State: I am not stuck with anything

## Progress


* We were informed by the scheduler team that there is no more need to set the dependency check and set bits in the compiler, instead the scheduler code will handle that based on the order and the contents of the packets provided.
* Continued work on packetization, we are now able to view the instruction DAG generated by PPCI using pydot https://media.discordapp.net/attachments/1413235564664062117/1432085834231845044/image.png?ex=69050b5d&is=6903b9dd&hm=18e0e7ffe3375107298cd32a2d33a798ac21dc94e9e463bd1b341ee5253039af&=&format=webp&quality=lossless&width=1228&height=308
* Created branch and PR for DAG visualization https://github.com/Purdue-SoCET/aihw-ppci-compiler/pull/8
* After visualizing the dag, we realized that instructions can be packetized first by the basic block they are already put into by PPCI (due to the jump order), and then they can be arranged into our VLIW by looking at each instruction's level within the dag. So when all instructions of level 0 have been issued, we can issue instructions of level 1 and so on.
* Received more guidance on how to instantiate vector registers: vector registers will have data loaded into them by SDMA, so we will need to first implement an intrinsic SDMA instruction. These SDMA instructions would take 2D arrays of bfloat16's, so we also need to implement that datatype. We can base a lot of that functionality off existing float logic in PPCI, or simply change the float datatype to consist of 16 bits instead of 32.


## Next steps

* Implement bf16 datatype and GEMM, SDMA intrinsics
* Organize instructions into packets based on level-ordering
